      "sentence": "The patient has profound hypotension, cold and clammy skin, decreased cardiac output, and high pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.",

      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Low cardiac output with elevated left-sided filling pressure and signs of poor perfusion indicates cardiogenic shock.",
      "grounding": "none",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Acute myocardial infarction and severe aortic stenosis can reduce cardiac output through impaired myocardial function and obstruction to left ventricular outflow, respectively.",
      "grounding": "passages",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": ["Neurology_Adams:002191"]
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response can also precipitate cardiogenic shock by shortening ventricular filling time and eliminating coordinated atrial contraction.",
      "grounding": "none",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, and sepsis primarily cause hypovolemic, obstructive, and distributive shock, respectively, so the best answer is I, II, and IV.",
